Not only comments, also submissions below a certain score. Adding proper nofollow's would help make voat less attractive to spammers. The only downside is that SEO-spammers would then have to use more annoying patterns instead of posting comments somewhere where they get ignored.

The spec distinguishes between comments by the content publisher themselves and third-party comments. However, in the case of Voat, the comments are the content. I would argue that submission links should have rel=nofollow, but not the comments. The main reason given for applying it to third party comments is to avoid incentivising spammers, but Voat has / can implement other methods of doing this. e.g. limiting the max comments per day for new / low CCP accounts. (Alternatively, you could just disable rel=nofollow for low CCP accounts.)
